proposal.title: One canonical target per occurrence segment. Never target a root.
proposal.detail: musaf_repetition_gevurot_open: in Hebrew, one local tei:p with an inline transclusion of urn:x-opensiddur:text:prayer:amidah/gevurot/attah_gibbor-mekhalkel_chayyim. In English, there are two local p's, one per existing literal segment: inline …/attah_gibbor, then inline …/mekhalkel_chayyim. musaf_repetition_gevurot_close: Hebrew and English each get one local p with inline …/mi_khamokha-mechayyeh_hametim. The relative range ends replace one trailing component, so both ends sit in rh_gevurot. musaf_repetition_yimlokh: Hebrew and English get inline urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:psalms/146/10, whose host is rh_vetimlokh. build.py:503-504 already gives that verse milestone the canonical corresp, because no source_reference_corresp is set. musaf_repetition_veattah_qadosh: inline bible:psalms/22/4 (see P2), then the existing literal segment ' אֵל נָא:' or ', O God.' as local words. musaf_uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah: inline …:prayer:uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah/text, not the root, which would bring in the host div, head and pb. Never target prayer:amidah/gevurot: its root is already mapped in another early Hebrew file. Targets carry @<language project> in documentary files.

proposal.title: Add the one canonical Ps 22:4 mapping in the existing Shacharit host, with no new file.
proposal.detail: In repetition_veattah_qadosh, segment 0 in both he and en: set corresp to urn:x-opensiddur:text:bible:psalms/22/4. Delete the context corresp …/veattah_qadosh/quotation/22/4, chapter_corresp …/quotation/22 and reference_unit. Keep source (the bounded tei:seg quotation) and keep end_reference:true. This takes the existing biblical branch at build.py:409-425: a bare chapter milestone (n=22; no corresp, because the chapter is neither the unit URN nor in complete_chapters), then milestone unit=verse n=4 corresp=bible:psalms/22/4. end_reference then calls close_references(), which writes a bare verse terminator and then a bare chapter terminator before segment 1 (' אֵל נָא:' / ', O God.'). proposal.title: Encode the occurrence wordings as j:option in the canonical host, using a separate reviewed overlay instead of editing the accepted host segments.
proposal.detail: Add a top-level readings.json list, wording_variants. Each entry has: id, host stem, lang, the host segment's identity (its corresp or source_reference, not an index), printed (exactly one occurrence in that fragment's literal text), and readings[] of {text, corresp: a condition URN}. Invariant: readings[0].text == printed. The host's own printed wording is then the first option, which is also what inline falls back to. Before emitting, the build merges each entry into the host fragment as the existing 'alternatives' structure. One build.py change is needed: in the alternatives loop at build.py:543-553, set option.set('corresp', reading['corresp']) when present. Today rubric_words ignores corresp, so the j:option corresp that PR311 selects on is never written. Spans needed (all verified against units.json): gevurot en, for ever|forever; falling and healing the sick and|falling, healing the sick, and; compassion, who remembers|compassion who remembers; in compassion.|in compassion;; And Thou|and Thou; O Lord who|O Lord, who. Ps146:10 he, יְהֹוָה|יְיָ and הַלֲלוּיָהּ|הַלְלוּיָהּ. Ps146:10 en, the Lord shall|The Lord will and Halleluyah!|Halleluyah.. Ps22:4 en, Thou, Holy One, dwellest|Thou, O Holy One, art enthroned. Uvekhen he, אַתָּה (הוּא) אֱלֹהֵינוּ|אַתָּה אֱלֹהֵינוּ (non-empty on both sides, so no empty j:option). Uvekhen en, And thus let sanctification arise for Thee, For|And therefore to Thee let holiness ascend for. Gevurot Hebrew and Ps22:4 Hebrew are identical and get no options. Name condition URNs after the wording, never after a service or recitation. Use one pair per canonical part per language, with every choice in that part sharing the pair.

proposal.title: Add a segment key 'canonical' that reuses the existing 'repeat' emission path, plus a unit key 'wording_selection'.
proposal.detail: Keep every literal fragment in each of the five musaf units unchanged as source evidence. Delete only the mapping fields: corresp, reference_unit, source, source_reference, source_reference_corresp and chapter_corresp. Add segment.canonical = <target URN>. In unit_document, handle it where 'repeat' is handled (build.py:483-489), after pb, instructions and speaker emission: write j:transclude type=inline target=canonical+'@'+project at fragment index 0, and write no words for that segment. Honour join_next instead of the unconditional trailing space, so ', O God.' spacing matches the current accepted output. Raise if a canonical segment has more than one fragment, or is combined with corresp, alternatives, quotations, qere_ketiv, expansion or abbreviations. Without that check, a later fragment's pb would land after the copied words. wording_selection is a list of opensiddur:variant fs, reusing feature_structures. Emit it as j:declare xml:id=<stem>_wording as the first child of the occurrence div and j:endDeclare as the last child, so they pair as siblings. Use the same list in the he file and the en file, holding both languages' features, so a parallel column compiled from either file is selected. The pb (with facs and printed n) and the speaker description (ח׳/חזן abbr-expan, 'חזן.' label) are produced by the existing code before the transclusion. They therefore remain occurrence markup and are never copied canonical words. Inline transclusion inside a local p keeps each printing's own paragraph count, for example he open = one p and en open = two p's.

proposal.title: Select the host's own printed wording where the host is transcluded, never inside the host file.
proposal.detail: Once the options are added, rh_gevurot, rh_vetimlokh, repetition_veattah_qadosh and uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah each contain unselected choices. An external compile of them with nothing declared would print both wordings, because PR311 keeps external alternatives when the selection is unknown. A j:declare inside the host file must not be used. Both processors run _handle_settings_element on declarations before the range start (see inline_compiler.py:198, which runs before the RECURSE check). The host's declaration would then be pushed after the occurrence's and win over it, so a musaf occurrence that inline-transcludes a host range would get the evening wording. Instead, derive host_selection = {readings[0].corresp: true for each overlay entry on that host}. Wrap the host's j:transclude in the 'unit' branches of documentary_order (build.py:990-993, which also covers the generated service 'file' documents) and of expanded_order (build.py:783-784) with j:declare/j:endDeclare. Use a per-file counter for xml:id uniqueness.

proposal.title: Keep old accepted payloads unchanged, and add new review keys for the new decisions only.
proposal.detail: unit_review_text (build.py:634-690) hashes fragment text, speaker, instructions and alternatives. It does not hash corresp, source, source_reference, end_reference, citation conditions or option corresp. Under P3/P4 the payloads of the five musaf units, the four host units and their citations stay byte-identical, so their existing reviews stay current without any hash being edited. That is legitimate only because the printed evidence really is unchanged. The new decisions are invisible to those payloads, so they need their own keys. variant/<id>: a payload of host stem, lang, identity, printed, and each reading with its corresp. occurrence/<stem>/<lang>: a payload of the canonical targets, the wording_selection features, any note-condition binding, and the literal text. Without --draft, require_review must demand both whenever a unit has canonical/wording_selection or a host has overlay entries. Add a build-time equality gate, extending the existing 'Documentary transclusion review is stale' check at build.py:876-882: resolve each canonical target in readings space (host segments carrying the start/end identity, inclusive), substitute the selected readings, and require .split() token equality with the occurrence's literal fragments, with identical Unicode normalisation. Never regenerate or overwrite existing review hashes as part of this change.

proposal.title: One mapping per prayer part and per verse in each language project. Remove the service-context identities.
proposal.detail: After the change, the only canonical mappings these units touch are: gevurot/attah_gibbor, /mekhalkel_chayyim, /mi_khamokha, /mechayyeh_hametim (in rh_gevurot); bible:psalms/146/10 (rh_vetimlokh); bible:psalms/22/4 (repetition_veattah_qadosh); prayer:uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah and /text (the existing host). Each is mapped once per language project. The occurrence files keep only their siddur: div corresp. Retire the now-unused siddur: context URNs: …/repetition_gevurot_open/text, …/repetition_gevurot_close/text, …/repetition_yimlokh/text(/quotation(/chapter)), …/musaf/repetition_veattah_qadosh/text(/quotation(/chapter)), …/repetition_uvekhen_lekha_taaleh_qedushah/text, and Shacharit …/veattah_qadosh/quotation/22(/4). Remove them from specs/urn_registry/siddur.jsonl in a paired PR; before the first stable release a URN is replaced outright, not aliased. The identity check (build.py:1011-1042) must add 'canonical' and split range targets at '-', validating the start and the resolved end separately rather than passing the range to registry.resolve.

proposal.title: Expanded edition: target the bare canonical through the existing section mechanism, with no new code.
proposal.detail: For each of the four units with full canonical coverage, replace {unit: stem} in expanded_order with {section: <name>, role: 'reader' where the print has a reader speaker, declarations: [the same wording_selection], order: [{reference: {target: <bare canonical>}}]}. Sections already emit the role note and j:declare/j:endDeclare (build.py:738-757). Caveat: a bare target resolves by priority [EXPANDED, dependencies…, he, en]. A dependency carrying the same URN wins, and its own wording applies. See the risks.

proposal.title: Stop the (הוא) commentary from following /text into Musaf.
proposal.detail: The uvekhen citation targets …/text, so inline transclusion would attach it to the Musaf occurrence, which omits הוא. Add citation.conditions = [{type: opensiddur:variant, features: {<הוא-wording condition URN>: true}}]. build.py:264-266 already emits this as j:condition. It is false only where Musaf selects the other wording, so the note is kept in the host and when the selection is undecided. Because citation review text does not include conditions, record this binding in the occurrence/ review payload (P6).

risks: Residual design blocker (ElNa): ' אֵל נָא:' / ', O God.' has no canonical identity. Keeping it as local words leaves a siddur: occurrence file holding liturgy, which fails the scheme's 'remove every j:transclude' test, though repetition_veattah_qadosh already does the same. It also means the expanded edition cannot reach ElNa by a bare canonical transclusion. Two choices: (a) accept local ElNa and let the expanded edition keep transcluding the occurrence for this one unit; or (b) register a top-level prayer: identity for the fixed formula ואתה קדוש יושב תהלות ישראל אל נא, with a prayer-part milestone in the Shacharit host enclosing the Ps 22:4 verse milestones and ending after ElNa. The user needs to decide this before implementation. (b) is the only route that fully satisfies the 'transclude canonical text' rule.

Inline flattening probably drops j:divineName, tei:seg/@source and other inline markup from the copied words. InlineCompilerProcessor merges same-language child text into its parent and does not keep the element. The printed words survive but the semantics differ from today's musaf files. This needs verifying. External transclusion keeps the markup but brings the host's paragraph count, which breaks the 'preserve paragraphs' requirement.

A j:declare inside a host file would silently override every occurrence selection (declarations before the range start are processed, and the later one wins). Add a build guard that hosts contain no opensiddur:variant declarations.

Unselected choices: a compile path into a host that is not wrapped by P5 prints both alternatives (external), or the host wording (inline). The tests must cover documentary, with_translation (parallel), expanded and electronic.

Bare canonical targets in the expanded edition can resolve to a dependency project. For bible: verses that could be a Tanakh witness with cantillation and different pointing, so Marmorstein's selection would not apply. Check what each target resolves to.

The existing review payloads omit corresp, source, end_reference, citation conditions and option corresp, so mapping-only edits are invisible to accepted reviews. P6's new keys are required, not optional.

corrections.json is applied by file path after the build. A correction aimed at words that move out of a musaf occurrence file would no longer find its target, or would need to become a host-level option. Not checked, because the file was not read.
A canonical range must not contain an ed=1965 pb from the host's printing. The current host data has none inside these ranges, but this should be enforced.
refdb must be resynced after the rebuild, or compiler.py's stale-index warning will appear and the new ranges will resolve to the wrong text.
The condition URNs are unregistered (opensiddur:variant is open). Names must describe wording only. Inventing service-time or recitation identities would contradict the instruction.
Under the scheme, where a shared text is realised may move later (for example Ps 22:4 into a Psalms or Kedushah home). The URNs stay the same, but the overlay entries would move with it.
